title: Unclog inflight-window saturation causing KV-deprivation and small-request suppression
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Production reports from three customers (two on Hosted, one on Dedicated) show sporadic latency spikes for short, single-shot requests while long-sequence workloads continue to progress. Root cause investigation points to the admission/inflight window calculation in the continuous batcher which allows long-context flows to monopolize inflight slots and trigger aggressive KV cache eviction, starving small requests and causing amplified tail latency. This ticket tracks the triage, corrective patches, and rollout for a safe remediation that preserves throughput for long sequences while restoring predictable latency for short requests across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Why different from previous fixes: Existing work focused on prefetch quarantine and admission hysteresis for obvious batch starvation patterns. This issue stems from a subtler inflight-window oversubscription when backlog snapshots are stale under bursty ingress: the scheduler over-allocates inflight capacity based on imprecise headroom estimates, creating 'inflight window saturation' that both blocks small fast flows and increases KV churn. The fix requires coordination between admission logic, KV pinning, and a small fast-path for tiny requests rather than only adjusting batch size heuristics.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy runtime-1.18 with continuous-batcher enabled on a 4-GPU host
Start a sustained stream of long-sequence requests (context length > 8k) from tenant A to occupy steady throughput
Introduce microbursts of short requests (prompt length < 64) from tenant B at 10x baseline rate
Observe: small requests see 5-25x token-latency spikes and timeouts while long sequences continue emitting tokens
Reproduce is easier when prefetch is enabled and eviction aggressiveness is default (no hysteresis)
investigation_notes: 11/03: Collected pprof and tracing from affected hosts; observed inflightSlots metric pegged and admission window growing despite queue depth fluctuation
11/04: KV eviction logs show repeated churn between tenant A and B leading to cache misses for small requests—eviction rate correlated with admission window overshoot
11/05: Experimented with limiting per-tenant inflight cap; small requests recovered but overall GPU throughput dropped by ~6% at high load
11/06: Reproduced sentinel case in a dedicated private environment where upgrade window caused batcher state reconciliation delays, confirming the state-staleness hypothesis
Observed that current admission uses a headroom estimate from a rolling snapshot updated on tick boundary; tick drift + microburst creates a gap where inflight can be oversubscribed
proposed_fix: Introduce an inflight-lease mechanism: each admitted batch occupies an inflight lease with a short TTL; scheduler reclaims expired leases to avoid permanent oversubscription
Add a tiny-request fast-path: bypass continuous-batcher admission for requests under token and latency thresholds and route to a low-latency worker pool (bounded capacity)
Implement KV pinning for recently-served small requests to reduce eviction cost during bursts (hot-key pin window of ~500ms), configurable per-deployment
Tighten admission headroom calculation with conservative safety margin when tick drift or snapshot age > threshold
Expose a runtime flag to toggle preemption policy and fast-path sizing for Dedicated customers who want deterministic throughput trade-offs
rollout_plan: Ship patch in runtime-1.19 branch behind feature-flag (ff:inflight-lease + ff:small-request-fastpath)
Canary rollout: 1% Hosted traffic -> 10% -> 50% over 48 hours with automated rollback on tail-latency regression
Dedicated: notify reserved customers and offer opt-in to early patch in a controlled maintenance window
Private: provide an upgrade bundle and post-upgrade validation script; offer runbook for on-prem teams to tune pin window
Post-deploy: 72-hour elevated telemetry with owner on-call (Arjun Patel) and a follow-up incident review scheduled
telemetry_and_checks: New metrics: inflight_lease_count, inflight_lease_expirations, small_fastpath_invocations, kv_pin_hits
SLO checks: 95th and 99th token latency for requests < 100 tokens must not regress beyond 10% versus baseline
Dashboards: per-tenant tail-latency heatmap and eviction-rate correlation panel
Alert rule: if small_fastpath_invocations > baseline*3 AND 99th_latency_short_requests > baseline*2 -> Pager
Add a deterministic replay canary to run synthetic mixed-length load every deploy (see canary-runner link)
comments: 11/02 Maya Chen: Triage call notes - customer A (hosted) reported sustained 95th token latency spikes starting 2025-10-30; initial mitigation increased admission conservative margin which reduced occurrences but did not restore SLOs
11/04 Arjun Patel: Reproduced locally; adding heap of traces to PR; preliminary fix using per-tenant inflight cap helps but regresses aggregate throughput under sustained long workloads
11/06 Priya Rao (SRE): Recommend inflight lease TTL approach to avoid manual cap tuning; suggested 250ms default TTL based on observed burst patterns
11/08 Engineering review: agreed to implement inflight-lease + small fast-path; Design owner: Arjun (runtime), Reviewer: Luis Gomez (scheduler)
11/10 QA: Integration tests added for lease expiry, small-path overflow, and KV pin eviction scenarios. Documented deterministic-replay steps in canary runner
11/11 Customer success: Customer B on Dedicated accepted scheduled maintenance for opt-in patch on 2025-11-18
11/12 Release lead (Nina Alvarez): runtime-1.19 branch is cut; flag gating in place; canary automation ready. Next: start 1% canary tomorrow
notes_for_docs_team: Console should surface inflight-lease metrics and provide per-route fast-path toggle. Update troubleshooting KB with delta between inflight cap and inflight lease approaches. Include recommended default values and tuning guidance for Dedicated/Private customers.
